items.rationale: The branches are fixed in the script, so the script owns the control flow; the model only supplies one label. Calling a model, or its reading of urgency, does not make it the one choosing the next step.
With a known sequence the chain makes only the model calls its stages need. A loop re-sends a growing history each turn and spends a further call to decide it is finished, with no stage to skip.
Running everything is slow and costly, and branches or presets cannot cover failure types that keep changing, so the model must choose the next check from what it has found.

items.rationale: When the model owns the control flow, a prompt rule is a request it may skip or reorder. A hard requirement must be enforced by code, either as a fixed step before booking or as a booking tool that refuses until verification has succeeded.

Keep the predictable, working paths as fixed code and give only the open-ended remainder to a model-run loop. Branches cannot cover varied, non-repeating questions, a better labeler cannot label what has no label, and a full loop adds cost to cases that already work.

A fixed chain has the same stages every run, so each has a known input and expected output that can be tested and rerun alone. Model calls inside stages still vary, and a loop's path differs from run to run.
